The compatibility response resolves the earlier migration concern, and no blocking defect was found. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `8028c729a643d0ba62480154d24ecbb3279d7755` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | A focused implementation with convincing live proof and compatibility coverage; no blocking findings remain. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** | Sufficient (live_output): The supplied AWS transcript exercises the changed Crabbox discovery and allocation path through a fresh Gateway, WSL2 enrollment, real agent execution, reconciliation, and successful reclaim on 0.53.1-dev. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (live_output): The supplied AWS transcript exercises the changed Crabbox discovery and allocation path through a fresh Gateway, WSL2 enrollment, real agent execution, reconciliation, and successful reclaim on 0.53.1-dev. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 9 items | Current main still excludes WSL2: The fetched main revision permits only Linux. Its Crabbox subtree and cloud-worker documentation match the pinned merge base, so the introduced WSL2 capability remains distinct.
Shared version gate precedes allocation: Discovery and provisioning share an in-memory version resolver. WSL2 preparation rejects unsupported or indeterminate versions before returning the allocation callback, and rechecks cancellation after probing.
Compatibility response is supported: The introduced changes contain no schema, migration, serialized-record, or persistence changes. Existing Linux defaults and allocation arguments remain intact; tests cover saved WSL2 defaults, placement overrides, old binaries, and Linux-only desktop/warm-image restrictions. These tests were inspected, not executed during this review. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together Cloud workers run session work on temporary machines while the Gateway retains the transcript and placement state. The Crabbox plugin translates profile and session OS choices into advertised machines and allocation commands. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Profile and session OS choice] --> B[Crabbox plugin] C[Backend catalog] --> B D[Binary version probe] --> B B --> E[Available operating systems and machines] B --> F[Version and profile checks] F --> G[Allocate and enroll worker] F --> H[Actionable rejection] ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge.

### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Compatibility surface** | 1 accepted OS value added; 0 new config keys or migrations | The capability extends existing selection fields without rewriting users' saved settings. | | **Production and test growth** | Production +98 net lines; tests +161 net lines | Production growth implements shared version gating and diagnostics, with boundary tests for compatibility and allocation rejection. | ### Stored data model Persistent data-model change detected: `migration/backfill/repair: extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-machine-options.ts`, `migration/backfill/repair: extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-provider.ts`, `migration/backfill/repair: extensions/crabbox/src/doctor.ts`, `unknown-data-model-change: extensions/crabbox/src/doctor.ts`. Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep OS support in the Crabbox plugin, using the existing selector and enrollment lifecycle while preserving Linux defaults. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Not applicable as a defect reproduction: this adds an intentionally unavailable target; current main's Linux-only restriction is directly visible in source. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes. Reusing the existing OS-selection contract and gating the plugin's advertised and allocated targets is a focused solution; no storage migration is needed. Its source configures the non-root worker, requires Node/npm during readiness, and preserves the distro between commands through the lease lifetime. ([`internal/cli/bootstrap.go:309`](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/blob/2db8380d3f9f1db79033200977c1b03f7c730b05/internal/cli/bootstrap.go#L309), [2db8380d3f9f](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/commit/2db8380d3f9f1db79033200977c1b03f7c730b05)) Likely related people: - **unknown:** The claimed source-line change could not be verified from bounded local history.
